items.title: Louis Cottrell, Jr. Interview, 1961-08-25
items.q: I heard Boca stayed on the session down at the Jean-Sami Hall... Peter Bocais and the father's name, they always called him Cottrell.

ctx.x: Well this to me suggests that there must have been a lot of drummers and bass players going on streetcars. They did.

If they weren't going on streetcars they would be walking. You take so many of the guys that walk from one engagement to another from their home. I heard Boca stayed on the session down at the Jean-Sami Hall, that drummer that he played with during that period was a fellow by the name of Veen. And Veen walked all the way up to the protection and I went back with his drum.

One funny story, I remember Natty Dominic, you know Don Albers of course. Yes, I know Natty too. His uncle, Natty Brave on Chicago. We got about six or seven tapes, the story of his life. Talked to him a long time and he started out on drums, I'm pretty sure. Maybe he had a few lessons with your father. Yeah, I know he talked about your father.
